response.message:
I've drawn a first IBM Cloud sketch for you to review. Support staff sign in through IBM App ID and use a Code Engine staff app. A Code Engine assistant service reads the synthetic tickets and reads CRM records without write access, searches approved knowledge in Databases for Elasticsearch filtered by what each person may see, and asks watsonx.ai to draft an answer that cites its sources. A person reviews every draft and decides whether to escalate, and nothing can issue refunds or change customer records. None of this is deployed or verified yet: these are proposed service choices, I haven't checked any IBM account or region, and no generator template covers this IBM design yet.

For the first local test, we'd run the app against the synthetic tickets, a fake CRM and a few sample knowledge files. A scripted stand-in would play the model, so the test only shows that the workflow, permission filtering, refusal rules and escalation path behave correctly. It says nothing about answer quality. Checking real grounding, accuracy and declining to answer when unsure needs actual watsonx.ai calls in an approved account, scored against agreed test questions.

Which country does the customer and ticket data need to stay in? That decides which IBM region we can propose.

proposal.title: IBM Cloud support-assistant first sketch
proposal.body: Scope: a staff-facing support assistant with authorized retrieval, grounded drafts written by watsonx.ai, a staff interface and human escalation. Assumptions: the ticket queue and CRM are existing synthetic systems that the assistant may only read. It never issues refunds or edits customer records. The region is not selected, and IBM account access, model availability and plans are unverified. This IBM workload has no native generator coverage yet, so it needs engineering.

data.label: Support staff
data.description: Support agents using a browser. This is an external client reference, not a provisioned service.

data.label: Staff sign-in
data.description: OIDC sign-in for staff. It issues tokens with the staff identity and group claims used for retrieval authorization. Federation with a company IdP is undecided.

data.label: Staff interface
data.description: Web UI that shows the ticket, the cited draft answer and customer context. Staff edit and approve or reject the draft, or escalate the ticket. Nothing is sent without a person.

data.label: Assistant orchestration service
data.description: Validates the user token, reads the ticket and the CRM record (read-only), and retrieves only knowledge the user is allowed to see. It calls watsonx.ai with the retrieved passages, checks that the draft has citations and declines to answer when evidence is weak. A hard-coded policy blocks refund and record-change actions. It writes escalations to the ticket queue only after staff approve.

data.label: Synthetic ticket queue
data.description: Existing synthetic ticket system. The assistant reads tickets and adds an escalation note or reassigns the ticket only after staff approval.

data.label: Existing CRM
data.description: Existing CRM with customer records. Read-only access with a scoped service credential stored in Secrets Manager. No write, refund or update permission.

data.label: Knowledge index
data.description: Holds chunks of approved knowledge with ACL and approval metadata. Queries are filtered by the caller's groups (keyword or hybrid retrieval to be decided).

data.label: Answer drafting model
data.description: Foundation model that writes grounded drafts from the supplied passages only. The model choice, its availability in the region, quotas and plan are unverified.

data.label: Approved knowledge store
data.description: Private bucket of approved knowledge articles with owner, approval and ACL metadata.

data.label: Knowledge indexing job
data.description: Scheduled job that reads approved articles from Object Storage, chunks them and upserts them with their ACLs into the index. It removes articles that are no longer approved.

data.label: Secrets
data.description: Stores the CRM and ticket-queue credentials and the service API keys. The diagram never holds secret values.

data.label: Logs and audit
data.description: Application logs and an audit trail of who saw which draft, which sources were cited, and every escalation or approval.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents financial loss and data corruption from model errors or prompt injection in ticket text.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: The assistant must not issue refunds or create, update or delete CRM customer records. Its CRM access is read-only, and ticket escalation happens only after explicit staff approval.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without this, restricted content could leak into drafts shown to the wrong staff.
requirementDrafts.statement: Retrieval returns only approved knowledge the signed-in staff member is allowed to see, and fails closed when the identity or ACL is unknown.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Ungrounded answers can mislead customers, and citations let staff verify the draft.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting ... and human escalation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Each draft cites the knowledge sources it used. The assistant abstains or escalates when evidence is insufficient, and a person approves drafts before use (proposed).

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: The emulation check had no failed tests. It stopped early instead: it never ran because eight components (App ID, the two Code Engine apps, Elasticsearch, watsonx.ai and the three existing systems) don't have a typed IBM implementation or an import plan yet. That's not a mistake in your design, and changing the diagram can't fix it. Building IBM support for those parts is product engineering work, and this report on artifact 3a368f33 can serve as the repro. The only IBM contract we support today is private Object Storage, so I've left the design as it is rather than shrinking it down to storage. Before anyone starts that engineering work, which country do the customer and ticket data have to stay in?
